sections.heading: Carried by more than one source

items.title: Introducing Clef: our open-source decision models, and new RL fine-tuning platform
items.blurb: We are introducing Clef and Clef-flash, open-source decision models hosted on Workers AI for high-speed classification and agentic workflows.

items.title: Introducing cf: the agentic CLI for the entire Cloudflare API
items.blurb: We are releasing cf, our new command-line tool that mirrors the entire Cloudflare API and supports programmatic TypeScript configuration. We are also open-sourcing Forge, our internal SDK generator.

items.title: Improving site performance by shipping more CSS
items.blurb: How we fully migrated github.com away from CSS-in-JS. The post Improving site performance by shipping more CSS appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

items.title: Four months of VoidZero at Cloudflare: making the open-source JavaScript toolchain faster for all humans and agents
items.blurb: Since joining Cloudflare, VoidZero has delivered more than 80 releases that drastically speed up JavaScript compilation, linting, and testing.

items.title: EmDash 1.0: the stable CMS with a secure plugin registry
items.blurb: EmDash 1.0 is a stable, open source CMS built for Astro, with agent-friendly workflows, secure sandboxed plugins, and a decentralized registry that keeps publishers in control.

items.title: Agents can now set up your website’s security with Turnstile Spin
items.blurb: Misconfiguring Turnstile by skipping backend validation leaves sites exposed to bots. Turnstile Spin fixes incomplete setups by using your preferred AI coding agent to wire up server-side verification.

items.title: Announcing Cloudflare OHTTP Gateway – expanding access to Cloudflare’s privacy-preserving infrastructure
items.blurb: We’re announcing the closed beta of a self-serve Cloudflare OHTTP Gateway. We’re also renaming our Privacy Gateway to Cloudflare OHTTP Relay to better distinguish the two products.

items.title: Rendering huge pull requests in the GitHub Copilot app
items.blurb: How we rebuilt the diff surface in the GitHub Copilot app to open a million-line pull request with hundreds of inline review comments. The post Rendering huge pull requests in the GitHub Copilot app appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
